# Introduction

This interactive R notebook provides a workflow for quality assurance and
quality control (QA/QC) of GEO-TREES tree inventory data. 

This notebook is provided as both a `.qmd` Quarto file, which we recommend
running in RStudio, and as a `.ipynb` Jupyter Notebook, which you can run in
JupyterLab either locally or on the ESA/NASA MAAP platforms. You can use either
version to QA/QC your data.

Each GEO-TREES acquisition contains one census of each plot, the __focal
census__, within a single site. The focal census is processed by the 
[GEO-TREES tree inventory data processing pipeline](https://github.com/GEO-TREES/INV_processing) 
to estimate above-ground woody biomass density (AGBD). The focal census should
normally be the census closest in time to the airborne LiDAR (ALS) acquisition,
either before or after. If you have data from other censuses of the same plots,
they can also be included in this QC workflow. Data from other censuses are not
used for GEO-TREES biomass estimation, but they can be useful for finding
errors in the focal census, e.g. implausible diameter growth, stems which were
missed, or taxonomic names which differ from previous censuses.

The notebook has two parts:

* [Part I](#part-i-focal-census-checks) checks the focal census on its own, 
  and previews how the GEO-TREES tree inventory data processing pipeline will use it.
* [Part II](#part-ii-multi-census-checks-of-the-focal-census) compares the 
  focal census to other censuses, to highlight issues affecting the 
  focal census.

The process for QA/QC:

1. Create a copy of your raw stem measurement data that conforms to the
   GEO-TREES L0 data format. See the [GEO-TREES Tree Inventory Guidelines, _Section 16: Data format_](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1Q5Wy_LbNEa0tNaGVntL0Bku41Z3t-TeU85_IxZuC6Uc/edit?usp=sharing). 
2. Open this notebook and load your __copy__ of the L0 tree inventory data.
3. Run the code chunks interactively in the notebook. Look at the outputs, and
   make changes to the input data where necessary. Changes can be made either
   by adding code to the notebook, or manually editing your __copy__ of the L0
   tree inventory data. 
4. Once you have finished working through the notebook, save and render the
   notebook as a HTML file. Note that all code in the notebook must run without
   errors for the file to render successfully. The method depends on whether
   you are using the `.qmd` or `.ipynb` version:
    * `.qmd` in RStudio: Run `quarto::quarto_render("INV_quality_control_nb.qmd",
      output_format = "html")` in the R console. You may need to run
      `install.packages("quarto")` first.
    * `.ipynb` in JupyterLab: Click `File > Save and Export Notebook As > HTML`
5. Send the following data to GEO-TREES for data archiving:
    * Original version of the raw data
    * Formatted raw data in the GEO-TREES L0 data format
    * Raw data with changes made following QA/QC, if fixes were applied manually.
    * The focal census stem measurement table written at the end of this
      notebook, `stem_focal.csv`
    * The completed `.qmd` / `.ipynb` QA/QC notebook
    * Rendered HTML of the QA/QC notebook 

# Setup

Install and load the GEO-TREES tree inventory QA/QC R package contained in this repository. This package
contains various convenience functions for flagging and optionally correcting
tree inventory data. The package will also load other packages as
dependencies. If you want to load additional packages to help you explore and
manipulate your tree inventory data, you can add to the code chunk below.

```{r}
#| eval: false
devtools::install_github("GEO-TREES/INV_quality_control")
```

```{r}
#| message: false
library(treeInvQC)
library(BIOMASS)  # Match taxonomic names to WFO `correctTaxo()`, fit diameter-height models `modelHD()`, wood density `getWoodDensity()`, AGB `computeAGB()`
library(ggplot2)  # Augment `plotScatter()` and `plotHistogram()` 
library(DT)  # Pretty tables in HTML notebooks

theme_set(theme_bw())  # Set default ggplot2 theme
```

```{r}
#| echo: false
# DO NOT EDIT
# Change default displayHelp rendering if compiled as HTML
if (isTRUE(getOption("knitr.in.progress"))) {
  formals(displayHelp)$html <- TRUE
} 
```

Throughout the notebook we display the help files for the different functions
in the notebook using the `displayHelp()` function. Below is the help file for
the `treeInvQC` R package:

```{r}
#| echo: false
displayHelp(treeInvQC)
```

## Create L0 tree inventory data   

Create a __copy__ of your raw stem measurement data that conforms to the GEO-TREES 
L0 data format. See the [GEO-TREES Tree Inventory Guidelines, _Section 16: Data format_](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1Q5Wy_LbNEa0tNaGVntL0Bku41Z3t-TeU85_IxZuC6Uc/edit?usp=sharing). 
__The original raw data should not be altered, always work with a copy of the data__.

You can use the [ATFS Data Harmonization Shiny app](https://github.com/Alliance-for-Tropical-Forest-Science/DataHarmonization) 
to help re-format your stem measurement data if you wish. The `inst/` folder in
[this repository](https://github.com/GEO-TREES/INV_quality_control) 
contains a `.rds` output profile for the GEO-TREES data format, which you can
load into the app. The app will walk you through creating an input profile for
your data, then performs the re-formatting procedure.

Alternatively, you can manually re-format your data, for example using a
spreadsheet editor, or in R.

The QA/QC code below requires you to supply the stem measurement table, the
plot meta-data table, and the plot geo-location table. 

You can also optionally provide a taxonomy table, stem height measurement
table, and wood density measurement table.

## Load data

Edit the code below to load your tree inventory data in the GEO-TREES L0 data
format.

Load stem measurement table, including all censuses of each plot. In addition
to the GEO-TREES L0 columns, the stem measurement table must contain an
`alive` column, with the mortality status of each stem measurement: `TRUE`
for alive, `FALSE` for dead, or `NA` if unknown. This column is used by many
of the checks below, but is not submitted to INV_processing.

```{r}
s <- read.csv("../../bicuar_test_data/out/stem.csv")
```

Load plot meta-data table:

```{r}
p <- read.csv("../../bicuar_test_data/out/plot.csv")
```

Load plot geo-location table:

```{r}
pt <- read.csv("../../bicuar_test_data/out/plot_pt.csv")
```

Optionally load taxonomy table:

```{r}
#| eval: false
tx <- read.csv("taxon_example.csv")
```

Optionally load additional stem height data:

```{r}
#| eval: false
h <- read.csv("height_example.csv")
```

Optionally load additional wood density data:

```{r}
#| eval: false
wd <- read.csv("wood_density_example.csv")
```

Columns which uniquely identify each stem measurement, each stem, each tree,
and each plot are used by many checks below.

With multi-census data, stem measurements must include the census ID
(`census_id`), which identifies the census of each plot. The order of censuses
is taken from `census_id`, so values must be integers which increase with each
census of a plot, e.g. `1`, `2`, `3`. By default, the last census of each plot
is the focal census.

```{r}
id_meas <- c("site_id", "plot_id", "census_id", "tree_id", "stem_id", "measurement_id")
id_stem <- c("site_id", "plot_id", "tree_id", "stem_id")
id_tree <- c("site_id", "plot_id", "tree_id")
id_plot <- c("site_id", "plot_id")
```

## Focal census

By default, the latest census of each plot is the focal census. To choose the
focal census of each plot yourself, e.g. the census closest to the ALS
acquisition, provide a dataframe to `focal`, with one row per plot, specifying
the `census_id` for each plot.

```{r}
focal <- NULL
# focal <- data.frame(
#   site_id = "Bicuar",
#   plot_id = c("P2", "P3"),
#   census_id = c(2, 3))

if (is.null(focal)) {
  # Latest census of each plot
  s$focal <- s$census_id == ave(s$census_id, s$site_id, s$plot_id, FUN = max)
} else {
  s$focal <- paste(s$site_id, s$plot_id, s$census_id) %in%
    paste(focal$site_id, focal$plot_id, focal$census_id)
}

message(sum(s$focal), " measurements in the focal census of ",
  nrow(unique(s[s$focal, id_plot])), " plots")

# Stem measurements in the focal census
sf <- s[s$focal, ]
```

```{r}
#| fig-height: 6
# Censuses of each plot, with the focal census highlighted
cens <- unique(s[, c("plot_id", "census_id", "census_date", "focal")])
cens$census_date_dec <- decYear(cens$census_date)

ggplot(cens, aes(x = census_date_dec, y = plot_id)) + 
  geom_line(aes(group = plot_id), colour = "grey") + 
  geom_point(aes(fill = focal), shape = 21, size = 3) + 
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("TRUE" = "red", "FALSE" = "white")) + 
  labs(x = "Census date", y = "Plot", fill = "Focal census")
```

### Data overview

```{r}
#| fig-height: 6
# Number of stem records in each plot census
ggplot(s, aes(x = plot_id, fill = factor(census_id))) + 
  geom_bar(position = "dodge", aes(colour = focal)) + 
  scale_colour_manual(values = c("TRUE" = "black", "FALSE" = NA), guide = "none") + 
  labs(x = "Plot", y = "Number of stem records", fill = "Census") + 
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1))
```

```{r}
#| fig-height: 8
# Composition of stem codes in each plot census. A sudden change in the focal
# census may indicate a change in field protocol or data entry errors
ggplot(s, aes(x = factor(census_id), fill = code)) + 
  geom_bar(position = "fill") + 
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::percent) + 
  facet_wrap(~plot_id) + 
  labs(x = "Census", y = "Percentage of stem records", fill = "Code")
```

# Part I: Focal census checks

The checks in this part use only the focal census, `sf`, which will be
submitted to the GEO-TREES tree inventory data processing pipeline.

## Data format 

`checkTableSpec()` checks your data against the column specifications in the
[INV_processing templates](https://github.com/GEO-TREES/INV_processing/tree/main/templates) 
and reports any issues. 

```{r}
#| echo: false
displayHelp(checkTableSpec)
```

```{r}
# `allow_extra = TRUE` allows columns which are useful during QA/QC, e.g.
# `census_id`. Only the columns in the specification are written to the focal
# census stem table at the end of this notebook
df_checkTableSpec_stem <- checkTableSpec(sf, "stem", allow_extra = TRUE)
datatable(df_checkTableSpec_stem)
```

```{r}
df_checkTableSpec_plot <- checkTableSpec(p, "plot")
datatable(df_checkTableSpec_plot)
```

```{r}
df_checkTableSpec_pt <- checkTableSpec(pt, "pt")
datatable(df_checkTableSpec_pt)
```

Rows with `severity` "error" must be fixed before the data can be processed.
Rows with `severity` "warning" can be fixed by coercing the column to the
correct class, e.g. `s$subplot_id <- as.character(s$subplot_id)`.

### Matching IDs among tables

```{r}
#| echo: false
displayHelp(flagTableMatch)
```

Every plot in the stem measurement table must be in the plot meta-data table,
and every plot in the plot meta-data table must have geo-location points:

```{r}
df_flagTableMatch_stem_plot <- flagTableMatch(sf, p, id_plot,
  comment = "Plot in stem table missing from plot table")
datatable(df_flagTableMatch_stem_plot)

df_flagTableMatch_plot_pt <- flagTableMatch(p, pt, id_plot,
  comment = "Plot in plot table missing from plot geo-location table")
datatable(df_flagTableMatch_plot_pt)
```

If you have provided optional tables, check that they match the stem table:

```{r}
#| eval: false
# Every taxonomic name in the stem table must be in the taxonomy table
df_flagTableMatch_stem_tx <- flagTableMatch(sf, tx, "taxon_name")

# Wood density measurements of taxa not in the stem table are not used
df_flagTableMatch_wd_stem <- flagTableMatch(wd, sf, "taxon_name")
```

### Plot area

```{r}
#| echo: false
displayHelp(calcPlotArea)
```

```{r}
plot_area <- calcPlotArea(pt, "plot_id", "x_rel_m", "y_rel_m")
datatable(plot_area)
```

AGB density is the sum of stem AGB divided by plot area, so an error in plot
area gives a proportional error in AGB density. If the plot meta-data table
contains the plot dimensions, check that they match the plot corners:

```{r}
#| echo: false
displayHelp(flagPlotArea)
```

```{r}
if (all(c("plot_length_m", "plot_width_m") %in% names(p))) {
  df_flagPlotArea <- flagPlotArea(p, pt, "plot_id", "plot_length_m", 
    "plot_width_m", "x_rel_m", "y_rel_m", tol = 0.01,
    comment = "Declared plot area differs from plot corners")
} else {
  df_flagPlotArea <- NULL
  message("Plot dimensions not in plot meta-data table")
}

datatable(df_flagPlotArea)
```

## Missing, duplicated, and phantom records

### Duplicated records

```{r}
#| echo: false
displayHelp(flagRecordDup)
```

```{r}
# Flag duplicated records based on ID values
df_flagRecordDup <- flagRecordDup(
  x = sf, 
  meas_id = id_meas,
  comment = "Duplicated measurement record"
)

datatable(df_flagRecordDup)
```

Duplicated records should be merged or removed. There should only be one
measurement for each concatenation of
`site_id`+`plot_id`+`census_id`+`tree_id`+`stem_id`+`measurement_id`.

### Duplicated stems

```{r}
#| echo: false
displayHelp(flagStemDupLoc)
```

```{r}
df_flagStemDupLoc <- flagStemDupLoc(
  x = sf,
  meas_id = id_meas,
  plot_id = id_plot,
  x_rel = "x_rel_m",
  y_rel = "y_rel_m",
  diam = "diam_cm",
  tree_id = "tree_id",
  dist = 0.2,
  diam_tol = 0.05,
  comment = "Possible duplicated stem"
)

datatable(df_flagStemDupLoc)
```

Stems with different tree IDs, almost the same coordinates, and almost the
same diameter, may be the same stem recorded twice, e.g. with an old and a new
tag. Duplicated stems are counted twice in AGB density.

### Missing values

```{r}
#| echo: false
displayHelp(flagValMissing)
```

```{r}
df_flagValMissing <- flagValMissing(
  x = sf,
  meas_id = id_meas,
  target = c(
    "site_id", 
    "plot_id", 
    "tree_id", 
    "stem_id", 
    "census_id", 
    "measurement_date", 
    "taxon_name",
    "code"
  ),
  cond = NULL,
  comment = "Missing measurement values"
)

datatable(df_flagValMissing)
```

Some columns must never contain `<NA>` values, particularly ID values. Stems
without a `code` are excluded from AGB estimates by INV_processing. Stems may
be missing coordinates, see [Trees without coordinates](#trees-without-coordinates).

```{r}
df_flagValMissing_diam_cm <- flagValMissing(
  x = sf,
  meas_id = id_meas,
  target = "diam_cm",
  cond = grepl("A", sf$code) & !grepl("T|F|M", sf$code),
  comment = "Missing diameter values"
)

datatable(df_flagValMissing_diam_cm)
```

Some columns are only allowed to contain missing values under certain
conditions. For example, living and standing stems should always have a
diameter measurement. INV_processing imputes the diameter of these stems by 
default, which increases the uncertainty of AGB density.

```{r}
df_flagValMissing_pom_m <- flagValMissing(
  x = sf,
  meas_id = id_meas,
  target = "pom_m",
  cond = !is.na(sf$diam_cm),
  comment = "Missing POM values"
)

datatable(df_flagValMissing_pom_m)
```

If a stem has a diameter measurement then it should have a Point of Measurement (POM) value.

### Values which should be empty

```{r}
#| echo: false
displayHelp(flagValPresent)
```

```{r}
df_flagValPresent_missing <- flagValPresent(
  x = sf,
  meas_id = id_meas,
  target = c("diam_cm", "pom_m", "height_m"),
  cond = grepl("M", sf$code),
  comment = "Missing stem with measurement values"
)

datatable(df_flagValPresent_missing)

df_flagValPresent_broken <- flagValPresent(
  x = sf,
  meas_id = id_meas,
  target = "diam_cm",
  cond = grepl("T", sf$code),
  comment = "Stem broken below POM with diameter"
)

datatable(df_flagValPresent_broken)
```

INV_processing stops if a stem recorded as missing ("M") has a diameter, POM
or height measurement, and warns if a stem broken below the POM ("T") has a
diameter measurement.

## Diameter and height measurements

```{r}
#| echo: false
displayHelp(plotHistogram)
```

Inspect the distribution of diameter measurements. Are all measurements larger
than the minimum diameter threshold of the plot? Are any measurements
unrealistically large? 

```{r}
# Plot a histogram
plotHistogram(
	x = sf$diam_cm[!is.na(sf$diam_cm)], 
	boundary = 0,  # Align bars with 0
	colour = "black",  # Make pretty 
	fill = "grey"
) + 
  xlab("Stem diameter (cm)")  # Add x axis label

# Summarise values
summary(sf$diam_cm)
```

Diameter distributions in natural forests normally decline steeply from the
minimum diameter threshold. Look for plots where the smallest diameter class
has fewer stems than the next, which may mean that small stems were missed,
or that the threshold in the plot meta-data table is wrong. Plotting on a log
scale makes the large stems, which dominate AGB, easier to see.

```{r}
#| fig-height: 8
diam_min <- p[, c("plot_id", "meas_diam_min_cm")]

ggplot(sf[!is.na(sf$diam_cm), ], aes(x = diam_cm)) + 
  geom_histogram(binwidth = 2, boundary = 0, fill = "grey", colour = "black") + 
  geom_vline(data = diam_min, aes(xintercept = meas_diam_min_cm), 
    colour = "red", linetype = 2) + 
  scale_y_log10() + 
  facet_wrap(~plot_id, scales = "free_y") + 
  labs(x = "Stem diameter (cm)", y = "Number of stems")
```

Compare the diameter distribution of live stems in the focal census to other
censuses of the same plot. The distributions should be similar, unless there
has been a major disturbance:

```{r}
#| fig-height: 8
ggplot(s[s$alive %in% TRUE & !is.na(s$diam_cm), ], 
  aes(x = diam_cm, colour = factor(census_id), linewidth = focal)) + 
  geom_freqpoly(binwidth = 5, boundary = 0) + 
  scale_y_log10() + 
  scale_linewidth_manual(values = c("TRUE" = 1.2, "FALSE" = 0.4)) + 
  facet_wrap(~plot_id, scales = "free_y") + 
  labs(x = "Stem diameter (cm)", y = "Number of live stems", 
    colour = "Census", linewidth = "Focal census")
```

```{r}
#| echo: false
displayHelp(flagDiamMin)
```

```{r}
df_flagDiamMin <- flagDiamMin(
  x = sf,
  meas_id = id_meas,
  plot_id = "plot_id",
  diam = "diam_cm",
  plot = p,
  plot_diam_min = "meas_diam_min_cm",
  cond = grepl("A", sf$code),
  comment = "Live stem below minimum diameter threshold"
)

datatable(df_flagDiamMin)
```

Stems below the minimum diameter threshold have their own AGB estimate in
INV_processing, but are not included in AGB density.

```{r}
#| echo: false
displayHelp(flagValRange)
```

```{r}
df_flagValOutlier_diam_cm <- flagValRange(
  x = sf,
  meas_id = id_meas,
  target = "diam_cm",
  threshold = c(0, 200),
  comment = "Diameter measurements outside range"
)

datatable(df_flagValOutlier_diam_cm)
```

### Large stems

```{r}
#| echo: false
displayHelp(flagBigStem)
```

```{r}
df_flagBigStem <- flagBigStem(
  x = sf,
  meas_id = id_meas,
  plot_id = id_plot,
  diam = "diam_cm",
  threshold = 0.05,
  cond = grepl("A", sf$code),
  comment = "Stem with large share of plot basal area"
)

datatable(df_flagBigStem)
```

A single data entry error in the diameter of a large stem can change plot AGB
density more than errors in many small stems. Check that the diameters of the
largest stems in each plot are correct.

### Height measurements

If height measurements are available, find potentially erroneous measurements
based on the relationship between height and diameter measurements. Heights 
are often not measured in every census, so height measurements from all
censuses are used to fit the height-diameter model. If you have provided a
separate height table, `h`, you can fit the model to those data instead.

```{r}
#| echo: false
displayHelp(flagModOutlier)
```

```{r}
# Fit a simple height-diameter model using the BIOMASS package, using height
# measurements from all censuses
s_h <- s[!is.na(s$height_m) & !is.na(s$diam_cm), ]

hmod <- BIOMASS::modelHD(
  D = s_h$diam_cm, 
  H = s_h$height_m,
  method = "weibull",
  bayesian = FALSE,
  drawGraph = FALSE)

# Flag outlier measurements using model residuals
df_flagModOutlier_height_m_diam_cm_all <- flagModOutlier(
  x = s_h, 
  meas_id = id_meas,
  mod = hmod$model, 
  x_var = "diam_cm",
  y_var = "height_m",
  threshold = 3,
  comment = "Height-diameter model outlier"
)

datatable(df_flagModOutlier_height_m_diam_cm_all)

df_flagModOutlier_height_m_diam_cm <- filterFocal(
  df_flagModOutlier_height_m_diam_cm_all, sf, id_meas)
```

```{r}
#| echo: false
displayHelp(plotScatter)
```

```{r}
# Create scatter plot with outliers flagged, and the fitted model
s_hd <- merge(s_h, df_flagModOutlier_height_m_diam_cm_all[, c(id_meas, "comment")], 
  all.x = TRUE)
hd_line <- data.frame(diam_cm = seq(min(s_h$diam_cm), max(s_h$diam_cm), 
  length.out = 100))
hd_line$height_m <- predict(hmod$model, newdata = data.frame(D = hd_line$diam_cm))

plotScatter(
  x = s_hd$diam_cm, 
  y = s_hd$height_m, 
  flag = ifelse(is.na(s_hd$comment), "Not flagged", s_hd$comment),
  alpha = 0.5) + 
  geom_line(data = hd_line, aes(x = diam_cm, y = height_m), inherit.aes = FALSE) + 
  labs(x = "Stem diameter (cm)", y = "Stem height (m)", colour = NULL)
```

These outliers are not necessarily errors, but do deserve closer inspection.

```{r}
df_flagValOutlier_height_m <- flagValRange(
  x = sf,
  meas_id = id_meas,
  target = "height_m",
  threshold = c(0, 50),
  comment = "Height measurements outside range"
)

datatable(df_flagValOutlier_height_m)
```

If INV_processing fits a local height-diameter model (`height_method:
"field"`), heights of the largest stems are extrapolated from the model if
there are no height measurements of large stems. Check that the height
measurements cover the diameter range of the stems, especially the large
stems which make up most of the AGB:

```{r}
diam_h_max <- max(s_h$diam_cm)
ba <- pi * (sf$diam_cm / 200)^2
ba_above <- sum(ba[sf$diam_cm > diam_h_max], na.rm = TRUE) / sum(ba, na.rm = TRUE)

message(sprintf(
  "Largest stem with a height measurement: %.1f cm. %.1f%% of basal area in the focal census is in larger stems",
  diam_h_max, 100 * ba_above))

h_cover <- rbind(
  data.frame(diam_cm = sf$diam_cm[!is.na(sf$diam_cm)], 
    data = "Stems in focal census"),
  data.frame(diam_cm = s_h$diam_cm, data = "Height measurements"))

ggplot(h_cover, aes(x = diam_cm, colour = data)) + 
  geom_freqpoly(binwidth = 5, boundary = 0) + 
  scale_y_log10() + 
  labs(x = "Stem diameter (cm)", y = "Number of stems", colour = NULL)
```

## Measurement precision

The checks in this section are run on all censuses, so that the focal census
can be compared to other censuses of the same plot, and then filtered to the
focal census.

### Unit mixtures

```{r}
#| echo: false
displayHelp(flagValUnit)
```

```{r}
df_flagValUnit_all <- flagValUnit(
  x = s,
  plot_id = "plot_id",
  census_id = "census_id",
  target = "diam_cm",
  threshold = 5, 
  cv_threshold = 100,
  comment = "Diameter unit-shift"
)

datatable(df_flagValUnit_all)

df_flagValUnit <- filterFocal(df_flagValUnit_all, sf, c("plot_id", "census_id"))
```

### Rounded values

```{r}
#| echo: false
displayHelp(flagValRound)
```

```{r}
df_flagValRound_diam_cm_all <- flagValRound(
  x = s, 
  census_id = c("plot_id", "census_id"),
  target = "diam_cm",
  precision = 1, 
  threshold = 0.3,
  comment = "Rounded diameter values"
)

datatable(df_flagValRound_diam_cm_all)

df_flagValRound_diam_cm <- filterFocal(df_flagValRound_diam_cm_all, sf, 
  c("plot_id", "census_id"))
```

`flagValRound()` finds groups with improbably high proportions of rounded
measurement values, which might imply poor measurement precision.

### Terminal digit preference

```{r}
#| echo: false
displayHelp(flagValDigit)
```

```{r}
df_flagValDigit_diam_cm_all <- flagValDigit(
  x = s,
  group_id = c("plot_id", "census_id"),
  target = "diam_cm",
  digits = 1,
  comment = "Terminal digit preference in diameter"
)

datatable(df_flagValDigit_diam_cm_all)

df_flagValDigit_diam_cm <- filterFocal(df_flagValDigit_diam_cm_all, sf, 
  c("plot_id", "census_id"))
```

```{r}
#| fig-height: 8
# Proportion of diameters ending in each digit, in each plot census. The 
# dashed line shows the expected proportion if digits are uniformly 
# distributed
digit <- data.frame(
  plot_id = s$plot_id, 
  census_id = factor(s$census_id), 
  focal = s$focal,
  digit = factor(round(s$diam_cm * 10) %% 10))
digit <- digit[!is.na(digit$digit), ]

ggplot(digit, aes(x = digit, fill = census_id)) + 
  geom_bar(aes(y = after_stat(prop), group = census_id), position = "dodge") + 
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0.1, linetype = 2) + 
  facet_wrap(~plot_id) + 
  labs(x = "Terminal digit of diameter (mm)", y = "Proportion of stems", 
    fill = "Census")
```

An excess of terminal digits 0 and 5 suggests that diameters were estimated
or rounded, rather than read from the tape. This increases diameter
measurement error, and may indicate that some stems were not measured.

## Point of measurement (POM)

```{r}
ggplot(sf[!is.na(sf$pom_m), ], aes(x = pom_m)) + 
  geom_histogram(binwidth = 0.1, boundary = 0, fill = "grey", colour = "black") + 
  scale_y_log10() + 
  labs(x = "POM (m)", y = "Number of stems")
```

```{r}
#| echo: false
displayHelp(flagPomDefault)
```

```{r}
df_flagPomDefault <- flagPomDefault(
  x = sf,
  meas_id = id_meas,
  plot_id = "plot_id",
  pom = "pom_m",
  code = "code",
  plot = p,
  plot_pom_default = "meas_pom_default_m",
  code_raised = c("U", "I"),
  tol = 0.05,
  comment = "POM inconsistent with plot default"
)

datatable(df_flagPomDefault)
```

```{r}
# POM against diameter. Stems measured above the default POM are normally 
# large, buttressed stems
ggplot(sf[!is.na(sf$pom_m) & !is.na(sf$diam_cm), ], 
  aes(x = diam_cm, y = pom_m, colour = grepl("[UI]", code))) + 
  geom_jitter(width = 0, height = 0.02, alpha = 0.5) + 
  geom_hline(data = p, aes(yintercept = meas_pom_default_m), linetype = 2) + 
  labs(x = "Stem diameter (cm)", y = "POM (m)", colour = "Raised POM code")
```

INV_processing can correct diameters measured above 1.3 m to their equivalent
at 1.3 m using a taper model. Stems measured above the default POM because of
buttresses should have the "U" code, and stems measured away from the default
POM because of irregularities should have the "I" code.

## Stem condition codes

```{r}
#| echo: false
displayHelp(flagCodeVal)
```

```{r}
df_flagCodeVal <- flagCodeVal(
  x = sf,
  meas_id = id_meas,
  target = "code",
  accepted = c("A", "D", "S", "F", "M", "B", "T", "U", "I", "H"),
  invalid_comb = list(
	c("A", "D"),
	c("S", "F"),
	c("B", "T")
  ),
  cond = NULL,
  comment = "Invalid code values"
)

datatable(df_flagCodeVal)
```

`flagCodeVal()` identifies measurements either with invalid values in the
`code` column, or invalid combinations or codes. For example, a stem cannot be
dead ("D") and alive ("A") at the same time, or standing ("S") and fallen
("F"). INV_processing stops if any of these are found. The valid codes are
described in the [INV_processing templates](https://github.com/GEO-TREES/INV_processing/blob/main/templates/stem_codes.csv).

```{r}
df_flagCodeVal_missing <- flagCodeVal(
  x = sf,
  meas_id = id_meas,
  target = "code",
  invalid_comb = list(
	c("M", "S"),
	c("M", "F"),
	c("M", "B"),
	c("M", "T"),
	c("M", "U"),
	c("M", "I"),
	c("M", "H")
  ),
  comment = "Condition codes on missing stem"
)

datatable(df_flagCodeVal_missing)
```

A stem which was not found ("M") cannot have its condition recorded. Only
"A" or "D" can be combined with "M", e.g. "AM" for a stem known to be alive,
but which was not found during this census.

## Measurement dates

```{r}
#| echo: false
displayHelp(flagMeasDate)
```

```{r}
df_flagMeasDate <- flagMeasDate(
  x = sf,
  meas_id = id_meas,
  plot_id = id_plot,
  date = "measurement_date",
  ref_date = NULL,  # Date of the matching ALS acquisition, e.g. "2024-03"
  max_diff = 1,
  max_span = 1,
  comment = "Suspect measurement date"
)

datatable(df_flagMeasDate)
```

```{r}
# Range of measurement dates in the focal census of each plot
ggplot(sf, aes(x = decYear(measurement_date), y = plot_id)) + 
  geom_boxplot(outlier.shape = 1) + 
  scale_x_continuous(labels = function(i) sprintf("%.2f", i)) + 
  labs(x = "Measurement date (decimal year)", y = "Plot")
```

GEO-TREES acquisitions should contain one census per plot, which should
generally be within one year of the corresponding airborne LiDAR acquisition.
Provide `ref_date` to check this. Measurement dates spread over a long
period within one plot may indicate that measurements from more than one 
census have been mixed.

## Stem coordinate issues

```{r}
#| echo: false
displayHelp(plotStemMap)
```

Inspect the spatial distribution of stems within each plot. Are any stems
outside the plot, or distributed unevenly within the plot?

```{r}
#| fig-height: 10
# Plot stem coordinates, sized by diameter
plotStemMap(sf, "x_rel_m", "y_rel_m", plot_id = "plot_id", diam = "diam_cm")
```

### Plot corner coordinates

```{r}
#| echo: false
displayHelp(flagPlotCorner)
```

```{r}
df_flagPlotCorner <- flagPlotCorner(
  pt = pt,
  plot_id = "plot_id",
  point_id = "point_id",
  x_rel = "x_rel_m",
  y_rel = "y_rel_m",
  x_proj = "rover_easting_utm_m",
  y_proj = "rover_northing_utm_m",
  threshold = 10,  # `corner_outlier_dist_m` in INV_processing
  scale_tol = 0.05,
  comment = "Plot corner inconsistent with stem map"
)

datatable(df_flagPlotCorner)
```

```{r}
#| fig-height: 6
# Residuals and fitted scale of all plot corners
corner_fit <- flagPlotCorner(pt, "plot_id", "point_id", "x_rel_m", "y_rel_m", 
  "rover_easting_utm_m", "rover_northing_utm_m", threshold = 10, 
  scale_tol = -Inf)

ggplot(corner_fit, aes(x = plot_id, y = residual_m)) + 
  geom_point(aes(colour = abs(scale - 1) > 0.05), size = 2) + 
  geom_hline(yintercept = 10, linetype = 2) + 
  labs(x = "Plot", y = "Distance from fitted corner position (m)", 
    colour = "Scale differs\nfrom 1 by >5%") + 
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1))
```

INV_processing fits a polygon to the GNSS coordinates of the plot corners to
place stems in their geographic location. Corners which do not fit the
relative coordinates of the other corners are removed, and if the area of the
fitted polygon differs from the area defined by the relative coordinates by
more than 5%, a warning is given. 

### Stems outside the plot

```{r}
#| echo: false
displayHelp(flagStemOutside)
```

```{r}
df_flagStemOutside <- flagStemOutside(
  x = sf,
  meas_id = id_meas,
  plot_id = "plot_id",
  x_rel = "x_rel_m",
  y_rel = "y_rel_m",
  pt = pt,
  tol = 0,
  comment = "Stem outside plot boundary"
)

datatable(df_flagStemOutside)
```

```{r}
#| fig-height: 10
# Map stems outside the plot boundary
sf_out <- merge(sf, df_flagStemOutside[, c(id_meas, "comment")], all.x = TRUE)

plotStemMap(sf_out, "x_rel_m", "y_rel_m", plot_id = "plot_id", 
  flag = sf_out$comment)
```

Stems outside the quadrat grid of their plot are excluded from quadrat AGB
density estimates by INV_processing, unless they are within
`outside_max_dist_m` of a quadrat.

### Stem coordinates relative to subplots

`correctLocSub()` checks whether XY coordinates match with subplot coordinates
and optionally re-locates incongruously located stems to the center of their
subplot.

If you have a table of subplot boundaries, e.g. `subplot.csv` for
INV_processing, use that as `subs` below. Otherwise, `inferSubplotBounds()`
estimates the boundaries of each subplot from the coordinates of the stems
labelled with that subplot. Stems from all censuses are used, as subplot 
layouts do not normally change among censuses.

```{r}
#| echo: false
displayHelp(inferSubplotBounds)
```

```{r}
subs <- inferSubplotBounds(
  x = s,
  subplot_id = c("plot_id", "subplot_id"),
  x_rel = "x_rel_m",
  y_rel = "y_rel_m",
  snap = 10  # Round boundaries outwards to a 10 m grid
)

datatable(subs)
```

```{r}
#| fig-height: 10
# Check that inferred subplots tile each plot without overlapping
plotStemMap(sf, "x_rel_m", "y_rel_m", plot_id = "plot_id", 
  flag = as.character(sf$subplot_id), subs = subs) + 
  theme(legend.position = "none")
```

```{r}
#| echo: false
displayHelp(correctLocSub)
```

```{r}
# Check if stem measurements located inside the correct subplot 
# according to relative coordinates and subplot ID.
df_correctLocSub <- correctLocSub(
  x = sf[!is.na(sf$x_rel_m) & !is.na(sf$y_rel_m), ],
  meas_id = id_meas,
  subplot_id = c("plot_id", "subplot_id"),
  x_rel = "x_rel_m",
  y_rel = "y_rel_m",
  subs = subs,
  subs_subplot_id = c("plot_id", "subplot_id"),
  subs_x_min = "x_min",
  subs_x_max = "x_max",
  subs_y_min = "y_min",
  subs_y_max = "y_max",
  tol = 1,
  correct = TRUE,
  comment = "Stem coordinates outside subplot"
)

datatable(df_correctLocSub)
```

```{r}
#| fig-height: 10
sf_sub <- merge(sf, df_correctLocSub[, c(id_meas, "comment")], all.x = TRUE)

plotStemMap(sf_sub, "x_rel_m", "y_rel_m", plot_id = "plot_id", 
  flag = sf_sub$comment, subs = subs)
```

Stems without coordinates are excluded above, as they are not located
outside their subplot. If `correct = TRUE`, stems outside their subplot are
given the coordinates of the centre of the subplot. In INV_processing, trees
without coordinates are placed at random within the extent of their subplot,
so stems with wrong coordinates or subplot IDs affect AGB density estimates.

### Trees without coordinates

```{r}
#| echo: false
displayHelp(flagTreeUnmapped)
```

```{r}
df_flagTreeUnmapped <- flagTreeUnmapped(
  x = sf,
  ind_id = id_tree,
  x_rel = "x_rel_m",
  y_rel = "y_rel_m",
  diam = "diam_cm",
  comment = "Tree without stem coordinates"
)

datatable(df_flagTreeUnmapped)
```

```{r}
# Percentage of basal area in each plot in unmapped trees
ba_plot <- aggregate(list(ba_m2 = pi * (sf$diam_cm / 200)^2), 
  by = list(plot_id = sf$plot_id), FUN = sum, na.rm = TRUE)
ba_unmapped <- aggregate(list(ba_m2_unmapped = df_flagTreeUnmapped$ba_m2), 
  by = list(plot_id = df_flagTreeUnmapped$plot_id), FUN = sum)
ba_plot <- merge(ba_plot, ba_unmapped, all.x = TRUE)
ba_plot$ba_m2_unmapped[is.na(ba_plot$ba_m2_unmapped)] <- 0
ba_plot$pct_unmapped <- 100 * ba_plot$ba_m2_unmapped / ba_plot$ba_m2

ggplot(ba_plot, aes(x = plot_id, y = pct_unmapped)) + 
  geom_col(fill = "grey", colour = "black") + 
  labs(x = "Plot", y = "Percentage of basal area in unmapped trees") + 
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1))
```

INV_processing places trees without coordinates at random within their
subplot or plot, in each AGB simulation. This increases the uncertainty of
quadrat AGB density, especially where large trees are unmapped.

```{r}
#| echo: false
displayHelp(flagIdNest)
```

```{r}
# Trees with stems in more than one subplot
df_flagIdNest_tree <- flagIdNest(
  x = sf,
  group_id = id_plot,
  parent_id = "subplot_id",
```


### Taxonomic resolution

```{r}
#| echo: false
displayHelp(flagTaxonLevel)
```

```{r}
df_flagTaxonLevel <- flagTaxonLevel(
  x = sf,
  meas_id = id_meas,
  taxon_name = "taxon_name",
  comment = "Stem not identified to species"
)

datatable(df_flagTaxonLevel)
```

```{r}
# Percentage of live basal area at each taxonomic level, per plot
s_lev <- merge(sf, df_flagTaxonLevel[, c(id_meas, "taxon_level")], all.x = TRUE)
s_lev$taxon_level[is.na(s_lev$taxon_level)] <- "species"
s_lev$ba_m2 <- pi * (s_lev$diam_cm / 200)^2
s_lev <- s_lev[s_lev$alive %in% TRUE & !is.na(s_lev$ba_m2), ]

ggplot(s_lev, aes(x = plot_id, weight = ba_m2, fill = taxon_level)) + 
  geom_bar(position = "fill") + 
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::percent) + 
  labs(x = "Plot", y = "Percentage of live basal area", fill = "Taxonomic level") + 
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1))
```

If you have morphospecies codes, check that they are consistently formatted,
e.g. "Brachystegia sp1" rather than a mix of "Brachystegia sp1" and
"Brachystegia sp. 1".

### Alternative growth forms

```{r}
#| echo: false
displayHelp(flagFormAlt)
```

```{r}
df_flagFormAlt <- flagFormAlt(
  x = sf,
  meas_id = id_meas,
  taxon_name = "taxon_name",
  family = NULL,  # Provide a family column if available, e.g. from `tx`
  growth_form = "growth_form",
  comment = "Possible alternative growth form"
)

datatable(df_flagFormAlt)
```

Palms, tree ferns, bamboos and other plants which are not dicot or conifer
trees should be labelled in `growth_form`. INV_processing can assign an
alternative allometry to these stems with `agb_allometry`, e.g.
"goodman2013" for palms, or exclude them from AGB density with
`growth_form_exclude`.

### Check taxonomic names against the World Flora Online database

```{r}
#| echo: false
displayHelp(correctTaxo, pkg = "BIOMASS")
```

```{r}
# The World Flora Online API is occasionally unavailable. If so, the rest of
# the notebook still runs, and this chunk can be run again later
df_correctTaxo <- tryCatch(
  BIOMASS::correctTaxo(
    unique(sf$taxon_name),
    interactive = FALSE,
    preferAccepted = TRUE,
    preferFuzzy = TRUE,
    sub_pattern = BIOMASS::subPattern(),
    useCache = FALSE,
    useAPI = TRUE,
    capacity = 60,
    fill_time_s = 60,
    timeout = 10),
  error = function(e) {
    message("Taxonomic name matching failed: ", conditionMessage(e))
    NULL
  })

if (!is.null(df_correctTaxo)) {
  datatable(unique(df_correctTaxo[df_correctTaxo$nameModified == TRUE,]))
}
```

### Wood density

INV_processing estimates wood density at the finest taxonomic level
available in the Global Wood Density Database, falling back to genus, family,
and finally the plot mean. Stems with genus, family or plot mean wood density
have more uncertain AGB estimates.

```{r}
# Estimate wood density for stems in all censuses, used below
taxon_genus <- sub(" .*", "", trimws(s$taxon_name))
taxon_species <- ifelse(grepl(" ", trimws(s$taxon_name)), 
  sub("^\\S+\\s+(\\S+).*", "\\1", trimws(s$taxon_name)), NA_character_)
wd_est <- BIOMASS::getWoodDensity(
  genus = taxon_genus, 
  species = taxon_species, 
  stand = s$plot_id, 
  verbose = FALSE)
s$wd_gcm3 <- wd_est$meanWD
s$wd_level <- ifelse(wd_est$levelWD %in% c("species", "genus", "family"), 
  wd_est$levelWD, "plot mean")
sf <- s[s$focal, ]
```

```{r}
# Percentage of live basal area at each wood density level, per plot
s_wd <- sf[sf$alive %in% TRUE & !is.na(sf$diam_cm), ]

ggplot(s_wd, aes(x = plot_id, weight = diam_cm^2, 
  fill = factor(wd_level, levels = c("species", "genus", "family", "plot mean")))) + 
  geom_bar(position = "fill") + 
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::percent) + 
  labs(x = "Plot", y = "Percentage of live basal area", fill = "Wood density level") + 
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1))
```

If you have provided local wood density measurements, check that values are
within the range of the Global Wood Density Database, which is used by
INV_processing for taxa without local measurements:

```{r}
#| eval: false
df_flagValRange_wd <- flagValRange(
  x = wd,
  meas_id = "taxon_name",
  target = "wood_density_gcm3",
  threshold = c(0.08, 1.39),
  min_n = 1,
  comment = "Wood density outside global range"
)

datatable(df_flagValRange_wd)
```

## Preview of AGB estimates

### Stems used to estimate AGB

```{r}
#| echo: false
displayHelp(flagAgbExclude)
```

```{r}
df_flagAgbExclude <- flagAgbExclude(
  x = sf,
  meas_id = id_meas,
  plot = p,
  missing_diam = TRUE,  # `missing_diam_method: "impute"` in INV_processing
  include_broken = TRUE,  # `include_broken` in INV_processing
  agbd_diam_min_cm = 0,  # `agbd_diam_min_cm` in INV_processing
  comment = "Stem excluded from AGB estimates"
)

datatable(df_flagAgbExclude)
```

```{r}
# Number of stem records excluded for each reason, per plot
ggplot(df_flagAgbExclude, aes(x = plot_id, fill = reason)) + 
  geom_bar() + 
  labs(x = "Plot", y = "Number of stem records", fill = NULL) + 
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1), 
    legend.position = "bottom", legend.direction = "vertical")
```

Check that stems are excluded for the right reasons. For example, live
standing stems which are excluded because they have no code, or many stems
excluded as "not standing", may indicate errors in the `code` column.

### Approximate AGB

To see which stems and plots will dominate AGB density, estimate the AGB of
each stem with the Chave et al. (2014) allometry, using the wood density
estimated above, and the location of each plot, as with `height_method:
"regional"` in INV_processing. These estimates are only approximate:
INV_processing combines the stems of multi-stemmed trees, propagates
uncertainty, and may use different height and wood density methods.

```{r}
# Longitude and latitude of the centre of each plot, from the plot corners
pt_cent <- aggregate(
  cbind(x = rover_easting_utm_m, y = rover_northing_utm_m) ~ plot_id + crs_epsg, 
  data = pt, FUN = mean)
plot_ll <- do.call(rbind, lapply(split(pt_cent, pt_cent$crs_epsg), function(y) {
  xy <- sf::st_coordinates(sf::st_transform(
    sf::st_as_sf(y, coords = c("x", "y"), crs = as.integer(y$crs_epsg[1])), 4326))
  data.frame(plot_id = y$plot_id, longitude = xy[, 1], latitude = xy[, 2])
}))

ggplot(plot_ll, aes(x = longitude, y = latitude, label = plot_id)) + 
  geom_point() + 
  geom_text(nudge_y = 0.002, size = 3) + 
  coord_quickmap() + 
  labs(x = "Longitude", y = "Latitude")
```

```{r}
# Estimate AGB for stems in all censuses, used below
s$agb_inc <- s$alive %in% TRUE & grepl("S", s$code) & 
  !grepl("[TM]", s$code) & !is.na(s$diam_cm)
coord <- as.matrix(plot_ll[match(s$plot_id, plot_ll$plot_id), 
  c("longitude", "latitude")])
s$agb_Mg <- NA_real_
s$agb_Mg[s$agb_inc] <- BIOMASS::computeAGB(
  D = s$diam_cm[s$agb_inc], 
  WD = s$wd_gcm3[s$agb_inc], 
  coord = coord[s$agb_inc, , drop = FALSE])
s$ba_m2 <- pi * (s$diam_cm / 200)^2
sf <- s[s$focal, ]
```

```{r}
# Stem AGB against diameter. Points far from the main cloud may be errors in
# diameter or wood density
ggplot(sf[sf$agb_inc, ], aes(x = diam_cm, y = agb_Mg, colour = wd_level)) + 
  geom_point(alpha = 0.5) + 
  scale_x_log10() + 
  scale_y_log10() + 
  labs(x = "Stem diameter (cm)", y = "Stem AGB (Mg)", colour = "Wood density level")
```

```{r}
#| fig-height: 8
# Share of plot AGB in each 10 cm diameter class
sf_agb <- sf[sf$agb_inc, ]
sf_agb$diam_class <- cut(sf_agb$diam_cm, breaks = seq(0, 10 * ceiling(max(sf_agb$diam_cm) / 10), 10))

ggplot(sf_agb, aes(x = diam_class, weight = agb_Mg)) + 
  geom_bar(aes(y = after_stat(prop), group = 1), fill = "grey", colour = "black") + 
  facet_wrap(~plot_id) + 
  scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::percent) + 
  labs(x = "Diameter class (cm)", y = "Percentage of plot AGB") + 
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 90, hjust = 1, vjust = 0.5))
```

```{r}
# Approximate AGB density of each plot
agbd <- aggregate(list(agb_Mg = sf$agb_Mg), by = list(plot_id = sf$plot_id), 
  FUN = sum, na.rm = TRUE)
agbd <- merge(agbd, plot_area[, c("plot_id", "area_ha")])
agbd$agbd_Mg_ha <- agbd$agb_Mg / agbd$area_ha

datatable(agbd)

ggplot(agbd, aes(x = reorder(plot_id, agbd_Mg_ha), y = agbd_Mg_ha)) + 
  geom_col(fill = "grey", colour = "black") + 
  labs(x = "Plot", y = expression("Approximate AGB density (Mg ha"^-1*")")) + 
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1))
```

Check that AGB density is plausible for the vegetation type of each plot.

# Part II: Multi-census checks of the focal census

__This part of the notebook should only be used if you have access to
multi-census data.__

The checks in this part are run on data from all censuses, `s`, and can find
issues in any census. `filterFocal()` then keeps only the issues which affect
stems or measurements in the focal census, `sf`. Issues in other censuses are 
kept in objects ending `_all`, which you may wish to inspect, but they do not
need to be fixed for INV_processing.

```{r}
#| echo: false
displayHelp(filterFocal)
```

## Stems missing from the focal census

```{r}
#| echo: false
displayHelp(flagRecordAbsent)
```

```{r}
df_flagRecordAbsent <- flagRecordAbsent(
  x = s,
  ind_id = id_stem,
  plot_id = id_plot,
  census_id = "census_id",
  status = "alive",
  focal = s$focal,
  comment = "Stem alive previously, absent from focal census"
)

datatable(df_flagRecordAbsent)
```

Stems which were alive in a previous census should be recorded in the focal
census, either with a new measurement, as dead, or as missing ("M"). Stems
with no record in the focal census may have been missed in the field or lost
during data entry.

```{r}
#| echo: false
displayHelp(flagRecordMissing)
```

```{r}
df_flagRecordMissing_all <- flagRecordMissing(
  x = s,
  ind_id = id_stem,
  census_id = "census_id",
  census_id_vec = NULL,  # Optional vector of census IDs
  plot_id = id_plot,  # Guess census IDs separately for each plot
  comment = "Missing stem measurement record"
)

df_flagRecordMissing <- filterFocal(df_flagRecordMissing_all, sf, 
  c(id_plot, "census_id"))

datatable(df_flagRecordMissing)
```

`flagRecordMissing()` finds stems recorded before and after a census, but not
in that census. Missing records should be added to the stem measurement
table.

## Stem IDs among censuses

```{r}
# Stems which belong to more than one tree, in any census
df_flagIdNest_stem_all <- flagIdNest(
  x = s,
  group_id = id_plot,
  parent_id = "tree_id",
  child_id = "stem_id",
  comment = "Stem in more than one tree"
)

df_flagIdNest_stem <- filterFocal(df_flagIdNest_stem_all, sf, 
  c(id_plot, "stem_id"))

datatable(df_flagIdNest_stem)
```

Stem IDs should be unique within a plot, so each stem should only ever belong
to one tree, in every census.

## Plot-level change

```{r}
#| echo: false
displayHelp(flagPlotChange)
```

```{r}
# Live standing stems
live <- s$alive %in% TRUE & !grepl("[FM]", s$code)

df_flagPlotChange_ba_all <- flagPlotChange(
  x = s,
  plot_id = id_plot,
  census_id = "census_id",
  census_date = "census_date",
  target = "ba_m2",
  cond = live,
  threshold = 0.05,
  comment = "Large change in plot basal area"
)

df_flagPlotChange_n_all <- flagPlotChange(
  x = s,
  plot_id = id_plot,
  census_id = "census_id",
  census_date = "census_date",
  target = NULL,
  cond = live,
  threshold = 0.05,
  comment = "Large change in plot stem density"
)

df_flagPlotChange_agb_all <- flagPlotChange(
  x = s,
  plot_id = id_plot,
  census_id = "census_id",
  census_date = "census_date",
  target = "agb_Mg",
  cond = s$agb_inc,
  threshold = 0.05,
  comment = "Large change in plot AGB"
)

df_flagPlotChange <- filterFocal(rbind(
  df_flagPlotChange_ba_all, 
  df_flagPlotChange_n_all, 
  df_flagPlotChange_agb_all), sf, c(id_plot, "census_id"))

datatable(df_flagPlotChange)
```

```{r}
#| fig-height: 8
# Basal area, stem density and AGB density of each plot over time. Focal 
# censuses are filled red
plot_ts <- aggregate(
  list(
    ba_m2 = ifelse(live, s$ba_m2, 0), 
    n_stem = as.numeric(live), 
    agb_Mg = ifelse(s$agb_inc, s$agb_Mg, 0)), 
  by = list(plot_id = s$plot_id, census_id = s$census_id, focal = s$focal,
    census_date = decYear(s$census_date)), 
  FUN = sum, na.rm = TRUE)
plot_ts <- merge(plot_ts, plot_area[, c("plot_id", "area_ha")])
plot_ts_long <- rbind(
  data.frame(plot_ts[, c("plot_id", "census_date", "focal")], 
    metric = "Basal area (m2/ha)", value = plot_ts$ba_m2 / plot_ts$area_ha),
  data.frame(plot_ts[, c("plot_id", "census_date", "focal")], 
    metric = "Stem density (stems/ha)", value = plot_ts$n_stem / plot_ts$area_ha),
  data.frame(plot_ts[, c("plot_id", "census_date", "focal")], 
    metric = "AGB density (Mg/ha)", value = plot_ts$agb_Mg / plot_ts$area_ha))

ggplot(plot_ts_long, aes(x = census_date, y = value, group = plot_id)) + 
  geom_line(colour = "grey50") + 
  geom_point(aes(fill = focal), shape = 21, size = 2) + 
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("TRUE" = "red", "FALSE" = "white")) + 
  facet_wrap(~metric, scales = "free_y", ncol = 1) + 
  labs(x = "Census date", y = NULL, fill = "Focal census")
```

Large changes in plot totals may indicate that part of the plot was not
measured, that stems were duplicated, that diameters are in the wrong units,
or that a disturbance event occurred, which should be described in the plot
meta-data table.

The same check within subplots can find subplots which were missed, or
measured twice:

```{r}
df_flagPlotChange_subplot_all <- flagPlotChange(
  x = s,
  plot_id = c(id_plot, "subplot_id"),
  census_id = "census_id",
  census_date = "census_date",
  target = NULL,
  cond = live,
  threshold = 0.1,
  comment = "Large change in subplot stem density"
)

df_flagPlotChange_subplot <- filterFocal(df_flagPlotChange_subplot_all, sf, 
  c(id_plot, "subplot_id", "census_id"))

datatable(df_flagPlotChange_subplot)
```

```{r}
#| fig-height: 10
# Number of live stems in each subplot in each census
sub_n <- aggregate(list(n_stem = as.numeric(live)), 
  by = list(plot_id = s$plot_id, subplot_id = s$subplot_id, 
    census_id = s$census_id), FUN = sum)

ggplot(sub_n, aes(x = factor(census_id), y = factor(subplot_id), fill = n_stem)) + 
  geom_tile() + 
  geom_text(aes(label = n_stem), size = 2.5) + 
  scale_fill_viridis_c() + 
  facet_wrap(~plot_id, scales = "free") + 
  labs(x = "Census", y = "Subplot", fill = "Live stems")
```

```{r}
#| echo: false

```

```{r}
df_flagDemogRate_all <- flagDemogRate(
  x = s,

# Intervals ending in the focal census
df_flagDemogRate <- df_flagDemogRate_all[
  paste(df_flagDemogRate_all$plot_id, df_flagDemogRate_all$census_t1) %in% 
    paste(sf$plot_id, sf$census_id), ]

datatable(df_flagDemogRate)
```

```{r}
# Mortality and recruitment rates in all census intervals. Intervals ending 
# in the focal census are filled red
demog <- flagDemogRate(s, id_stem, id_plot, "census_id", "census_date", 
  "alive", threshold = -Inf)
demog$focal <- paste(demog$plot_id, demog$census_t1) %in% 
  paste(sf$plot_id, sf$census_id)
demog_long <- rbind(
  data.frame(demog[, c("plot_id", "census_t1", "focal")], 
    rate = "Mortality", value = demog$mort_ann),
  data.frame(demog[, c("plot_id", "census_t1", "focal")], 
    rate = "Recruitment", value = demog$recr_ann))

ggplot(demog_long, aes(x = plot_id, y = 100 * value)) + 
  geom_point(aes(fill = focal), shape = 21, size = 2.5) + 
  geom_hline(yintercept = 5, linetype = 2) + 
  scale_fill_manual(values = c("TRUE" = "red", "FALSE" = "white")) + 
  facet_wrap(~rate, ncol = 1) + 
  labs(x = "Plot", y = "Annual rate (%)", fill = "Ends in focal census") + 
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1))
```

High mortality may indicate stems which were missed or retagged. High
recruitment may indicate stems which were missed in the previous census, a
change in the minimum diameter threshold, or retagged stems.

## Diameter timeline

```{r}
# Annual diameter growth of live stems between consecutive censuses, with 
# the same POM
g <- s[s$alive %in% TRUE & !is.na(s$diam_cm), 
  c(id_stem, "census_id", "census_date", "diam_cm", "pom_m", "focal")]
g$date <- decYear(g$census_date)
g <- g[do.call(order, g[, c(id_stem, "date")]), ]
g_key <- do.call(paste, g[, id_stem])
same <- c(FALSE, g_key[-1] == g_key[-length(g_key)]) & 
  c(FALSE, g$pom_m[-1] == g$pom_m[-nrow(g)]) %in% TRUE
g$diam_prev <- ifelse(same, c(NA, g$diam_cm[-nrow(g)]), NA)
g$growth_cm_yr <- ifelse(same, 
  (g$diam_cm - g$diam_prev) / (g$date - c(NA, g$date[-nrow(g)])), NA)
g <- g[!is.na(g$growth_cm_yr), ]
```

```{r}
#| fig-height: 8
# Growth against diameter in the previous census. The dashed lines show the 
# growth thresholds used by `correctDiameterSeries()` below
ggplot(g, aes(x = diam_prev, y = growth_cm_yr, colour = focal)) + 
  geom_point(alpha = 0.4) + 
  geom_hline(yintercept = c(-2, 4), linetype = 2) + 
  scale_colour_manual(values = c("TRUE" = "red", "FALSE" = "grey50")) + 
  facet_wrap(~plot_id) + 
  labs(x = "Diameter in previous census (cm)", 
    y = expression("Diameter growth (cm y"^-1*")"), 
    colour = "Ends in focal census")
```

```{r}
#| echo: false
displayHelp(correctDiameterSeries)
```

```{r}
df_correctDiameterSeries_all <- correctDiameterSeries(
  x = s,
  ind_id = id_stem,
  plot_id = id_plot,
  census_date = "census_date",
  diam = "diam_cm",
  status = "alive",
  pom = "pom_m",
  growth_thresh = c(-2, 4),
  n_stem_thresh = 3, 
  digits = 1,
  method = c("shift", "pairwise"),
  shift_anchor = "longest",  # Majority of the diameter timeline is correct
  comment = "Diameter timelines corrected"
)

df_correctDiameterSeries <- filterFocal(df_correctDiameterSeries_all, sf, 
  c(id_stem, "census_date"))

datatable(df_correctDiameterSeries)
```

```{r}
# Diameter timelines of the stems with the largest corrections in the focal
# census
cor_top <- df_correctDiameterSeries[
  order(-abs(df_correctDiameterSeries$diam_cor - df_correctDiameterSeries$diam_cm)), ]
cor_top <- cor_top[!is.na(cor_top$diam_cm), ][seq_len(min(6, nrow(cor_top))), ]

if (nrow(cor_top) > 0) {
  cor_plots <- plotDiameterCorrections(s, cor_top, id_stem, "census_date", 
    "diam_cm", pom = "pom_m")
  for (i in cor_plots) {
    print(i)
  }
}
```

Corrected diameters are suggestions. Check the field data sheets for each
stem before changing diameters in the focal census.

Write the focal census stem measurement table to submit to INV_processing,
with only the columns in the INV_processing specification, and check it
again:

```{r}
stem_cols <- read.csv(
  "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/GEO-TREES/INV_processing/main/templates/stem_cols.csv", 
  fileEncoding = "UTF-8-BOM")

s_out <- sf[, intersect(stem_cols$column_name, names(sf))]

df_checkTableSpec_out <- checkTableSpec(s_out, stem_cols)
datatable(df_checkTableSpec_out)

write.csv(s_out, "./stem_focal.csv", row.names = FALSE)
```

There should be no "error" rows above before the focal census is submitted.
